resources.string: A simple private diary for periods. It helps you remember dates and gives a careful guess about what may happen next. All data stays on your device.
Choose one answer before you continue. You can change it later. This helps the app avoid false exact dates.
Choose the option above that best fits your periods now. Until you do, the app will use a wide date range and will not guess a day when an egg may be released.
My periods started less than 1 year ago
In the first year, periods often come after a different number of days each time. That can be normal. The app will use a wide date range instead of pretending it knows one exact day.
During the first few years, periods can still come earlier or later from month to month. The app will allow for that.
My periods have been coming for more than 3 years and the gaps are usually similar
The app will learn from your recent dates. If the gaps stay fairly similar, the date range may become narrower.
My periods have been coming for more than 3 years but the gaps still change a lot
The app will use a wide date range and will not guess a day when an egg may be released. If you have never talked with a doctor about very uneven periods, it can be worth doing.
My periods are changing as I get older
As periods get closer to stopping for good, they may come earlier, later, or skip months. The app will use a wider range and will not guess a day when an egg may be released.
My periods stopped for a full year as I got older

Choose this only if the year-long stop is part of getting older, or a doctor told you the periods have stopped for good. If they stopped for another reason, choose the closest other option and talk with a doctor.
Choose the first day when the bleeding looked like your usual period, not just a few spots.
About how many days are there\nbetween your periods?
Count from the first day of one real period to the first day of the next. For example, from the 1st to the 29th is 28 days.
It is fine if you are not sure. Pick the closest number you know. The app will learn from the dates you add.

Use this choice only when periods have stopped for a full year as part of getting older, or a doctor told you they have stopped for good. The app will keep your diary but will not guess another period. If periods stopped for another reason, go back, choose the closest other answer and talk with a doctor.
day since the last period started
This is only a count of days. It does not tell us exactly what your body is doing today.
Your next period may start around
The app is keeping your records without trying to guess a next period.
Choose what best describes your periods in Settings. Until then, the app keeps the date range deliberately wide.
This is a rough first guess. Add more real dates and the app will learn your pattern.
Your recent gaps change quite a lot, so the app shows a wider range instead of one exact day.
Your recent gaps may be fairly steady, but their usual length is outside the common range for this stage. The app therefore keeps the guess wider and does not guess egg-release days.
This range is based on your recent recorded periods. It is still only a guess.
Days when pregnancy may be more likely
You are inside the rough calendar range
This is only a calendar guess. The app cannot know exactly when an egg is released. Never use these dates as “safe days” to avoid pregnancy.
Choose what best describes your periods in Settings. Until you do, the app will use a wide date range and will not guess a day when an egg may be released.

Your periods started recently. In the first year it is common for them to come after a different number of days each time. Keep recording the real dates; the app will not force them into a 28-day pattern.
In the first few years, periods can still come earlier or later from month to month. Keep recording what really happens.
You said the gaps between your periods usually change a lot. The app will keep showing what really happens and use a wide date range instead of forcing a fixed pattern.
As periods get closer to stopping for good, the gaps between them often change. The app therefore uses a wide date range and does not guess a day when an egg may be released.

You chose that periods stopped for a full year as you got older. The app will not guess another period. If that year-long stop happened for another reason and a doctor has not explained it, talk with a doctor.
There has been a gap of about 3 months or more. In the first years after periods begin, such a long gap is worth discussing with a doctor or another trusted health professional.
There has been no period for about 3 months or more. If pregnancy is not expected and you do not know why the periods stopped, it is worth talking with a doctor.
New bleeding was recorded after about a year or more without a period. Please tell a doctor about this bleeding, even if there is only a little.
This bleeding has lasted longer than is usual. If it is still going, is very heavy, makes you weak or dizzy, or worries you, ask a trusted adult or doctor for help.
This gap is shorter or longer than is common at this stage. One unusual gap does not tell you why. If this keeps happening or worries you, talk with a doctor.
Pale colors are guesses from past dates. Your body does not have to follow them.
Choose “A few spots” when there is only a little blood and it does not look like your usual period. A few spots will not start a new cycle in the app.
Write anything you want to remember…
Shortest and longest differ by about %1$d days
There are not enough recent finished cycles for averages yet. Your recorded history is still shown below.
Choose what best describes your periods in Settings. Until then, the numbers below are shown only as your recorded history and the app will avoid narrower cycle assumptions.
In the first year after periods begin, uneven gaps are common. The numbers below are a diary summary, not a rule your body must follow.
During the first few years, the gaps can still change. The app shows what happened instead of judging it against a 28-day cycle.
These numbers describe your own recent history. If your pattern suddenly changes or worries you, the app cannot tell you why.
You said your gaps have stayed very different even after the first few years. The app shows the real numbers without calling them a fixed cycle.
When periods are getting closer to stopping for good, the gaps often change and skipped months become more common. The app simply shows what happened.
You chose that periods stopped for a full year as you got older. The old history stays here, but the app does not guess another period.
Choose what fits now. You can change this at any time without deleting old records.

A private period diary that learns from your own dates. It shows date ranges instead of claiming to know an exact next period or egg-release day. It is not a medical test.
Your period records stay on this device unless you choose to save a CSV copy
This will delete all period records and settings from the app. It cannot be undone.
